title: podosemum glomeratum
intro: Podosemum glomeratum, commonly known as East Indian thyme or Pudina, is a plant species native to the tropical regions of Asia and Africa, belonging to the family Lamiaceae. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which help in treating digestive issues, respiratory problems, and skin infections. The therapeutic actions of Podosemum glomeratum include its use as an antiseptic, antispasmodic, and expectorant, making it effective in relieving symptoms of coughs, colds, and fever. The bioactive constituents of Podosemum glomeratum include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, which contribute to its medicinal properties and health benefits.
